design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.what_was_rejected: Rebinding the ledger actor_id COLUMN to the server-derived principal. This is the obvious fix and it is WRONG.
design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.how_it_was_settled: Two adversarial review lenses reached OPPOSITE conclusions - a correctness lens recommended rebinding the column, a security lens called it a blocking contradiction. KERNEL_BUILDER read the source rather than taking either: test_e7_swarm_edit_proof.rs:2944-2973 runs a DO block asserting kernel_event_ledger.actor_id = {app_attribution.actor_id}, which is the CLIENT-declared per-agent id, and :2866-2881 asserts assert_ne!(recorder_actor, save_actor_id). Rebinding the column fails AC-120-3 and AC-120-2 at the same time. The security lens was right.
design_decision_settled_by_direct_inspec.what_was_done_instead: The save route optionally authenticates via stage::capture_context and stamps the SERVER-DERIVED principal into the SERVER-WRITTEN receipt payload as minted_by_principal. validate_document_save_receipt compares THAT field against event.canonical_actor_id(). Ownership lives in the payload; per-agent attribution stays in the actor_id column.

implementation_result.non_weakening_verification_by_kernel_bui: Verified by reading flight_recorder.rs:885-940 directly, not accepted from the sub-agent report. The comparison is an UNCONDITIONAL conjunct of the authentic expression - no if, no ||, no unwrap_or(true). Absent, blank or non-string minted_by_principal fails CLOSED, and a blank claiming actor can never match a blank minted principal. Every other conjunct is byte-identical: event_type, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, actor_kind, kernel_task_run_id, session_run_id, correlation, the "saved" discriminator, workspace_id, content_hash. The old client-column comparison is absent from the file.
implementation_result.ac_120_1_PROVEN: mt120_authenticated_save_stamps_derived_principal_without_rebinding_actor_id asserts byte-equality between the save receipt minted_by_principal and the principal an INDEPENDENT capture_context-gated route (Stage) derives from the same binding. Deliberately not a local digest recomputation: the first attempt did recompute locally and produced a FALSE RED because serde_json::Value key ordering differs from the typed enum serialization - the product was correct and the test was wrong.
implementation_result.ac_120_2_PROVEN: Cross-principal receipt is unclaimable (400) with ZERO ledger and FR residue, and the SAME envelope succeeds once the receipt is minted by the claimant - proving the rejection was the principal and not an unrelated clause. Absent/empty/whitespace minted_by_principal also unclaimable. The ledger actor_id column is asserted == the per-agent id AND != the derived principal, so attribution is provably intact. Nothing was deleted or relaxed.
implementation_result.backward_compatibility: A save with NO session token behaves exactly as before: it succeeds, but its receipt carries no anchor and is unclaimable. This is what keeps app/src (a forbidden path for this MT) and roughly 28 tokenless test call sites working without a scope breach. A token that is PRESENT but invalid or stale is 401 HSK-401-DOC-SESSION and never downgrades to the header identity - that silent fallback was identified in advance as the single most dangerous shape this change could take.
implementation_result.namespace_guard: A client x-hsk-actor-id in the reserved handshake-native: namespace is 403 HSK-403-DOC-ACTOR-SPOOF on every document route unless it equals the principal the server just derived. Without this the derived principal would become a bearer-equivalent label an unauthenticated caller could stamp - the MT contract own positive control proved that works today.
implementation_result.run_ids_untouched_on_purpose: kernel_task_run_id, session_run_id and correlation_id are compared against the CLIENT-supplied FR payload. Adopting capture_context own run ids (the shape api::memory middleware uses) would have replaced one unsatisfiable clause with three.

scope.summary: Make the document_saved receipt-ownership check enforceable by authenticating the document-save route as the same principal the Flight Recorder derives, instead of leaving a clause that rejects every legitimate save.

defect_detail.why_unsatisfiable: The recorder actor is SERVER-DERIVED as handshake-native:{pid}:{birth_fingerprint} by capture_context. POST/PUT /knowledge/documents... has NO session authentication and takes its actor from a client header (backend_client::DOC_ACTOR_ID = handshake-native-editor). No route exposes the derived identity, so the frontend cannot stamp it. The two values can never match for a real product save.
defect_detail.runtime_evidence: Real save then document_saved ingestion with a genuine token and all fields matching => HTTP 400 HSK-400-INVALID-EVENT. Same session, undo_fired => HTTP 200. Positive control: issuing the save with x-hsk-actor-id set to the server-derived actor makes ingestion return HTTP 200 - proving the clause is the SOLE blocker.
defect_detail.security_framing: MT-109 intent is that a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it, which requires BOTH endpoints to authenticate the same principal. Today only one does, so the clause does not enforce the invariant - it rejects everything legitimate. A guard that always fails is an outage wearing a security control costume, and it also trains future implementers to weaken it.

acceptance_criteria: AC-120-1: the document-save route authenticates the SAME principal the Flight Recorder derives, OR the derived identity is exposed through a route the frontend can legitimately use. The clause must become SATISFIABLE without being removed.

AC-120-2: THE BINDING IS NOT WEAKENED. A save receipt minted by principal A must still be unclaimable by principal B - prove it with a negative test. Deleting or relaxing the actor comparison is an automatic rejection of this MT.
AC-120-3: test_e7_swarm_edit_proof goes green, closing the MT-115 PT-115-1 blocker (it is currently 24 passed / 1 failed).
AC-120-4: test_flight_recorder_authz still passes unchanged at 12 tests - the MT-109 negative suite must not regress.
AC-120-5: a real end-to-end product save emits document_saved and it INGESTS at runtime, proven live rather than in a stub.

It requires three mirrored emissions and currently receives two, because document_saved is rejected at ingestion (confirmed: zero document_saved rows in the ledger against 8 each for canvas_node_placed and undo_fired). If this MT is fixed correctly the third emission lands on its own.
